purpose: This tool lets you aim a line through a point P so it is parallel or perpendicular to a blue line. You will see that parallel lines have equal slopes, and perpendicular slopes multiply to -1.

stops.title: The graph
stops.text: Drag the ring at the end of your line to aim it. Drag P to move the point. Drag the two rings on the blue line: one slides it, one tilts it. Your line turns green when it is parallel and red when it is perpendicular.
stops.try: Drag your line's ring until it turns green.

stops.title: Challenge
stops.text: These buttons give you a goal. Make it parallel or Make it perpendicular, then drag your line to try. Show me does it for you and explains the moves. New line and point gives you a fresh puzzle.
stops.try: Press Make it perpendicular and aim your line.

stops.title: Blue line shortcuts
stops.text: These turn the blue line flat or upright. A flat line has slope 0 and an upright line has no slope at all. The rule that slopes multiply to -1 does not work for them, so look at what happens instead.
stops.try: Press Vertical and see what the perpendicular line becomes.

stops.title: Show helpers
stops.text: These switches turn extra things on the graph on and off: the answer lines through P, the slope triangles (rise over run), and the point where your line crosses the y-axis. The last one adds an equation quiz.
stops.try: Turn on Slope triangles and compare rise and run on both lines.

stops.title: What Next does
stops.text: Step 1 is parallel lines. Step 2 turns a triangle a quarter turn to find the perpendicular slope. Step 3 writes the equation through P and asks you to pick it. Step 4 uses flat and upright lines.

stops.title: Quick check
stops.text: Two questions at the end. A wrong answer explains why.

teacher: Project step 2 and ask what happens to rise and run when you turn a slope triangle a quarter turn. Many students think perpendicular means the opposite slope, so -2/3 instead of -3/2. Let them aim it and see the line fail to turn red.
